settings.title: Settings
settings.description: How OneOhm works: who can do what, the company details on every document, and the products and rates behind every price.
settings.noAccess: You do not have permission to change settings.

roles.intro: Each role is a bundle of permissions. Turn one on or off in its cell, or open a role from its name to rename or archive it; people pick up the change on their next action.
roles.members: {count, plural, =0 {No one} one {# person} other {# people}}

editor.name: Role name
editor.kindHint: Staff see company data by permission. Partners and resellers only ever see their own work.
editor.kindLocked: The kind is fixed once a role is created.
editor.protectedNote: Super Admin always holds every permission and cannot be changed or archived, so there is always someone who can fix access.
editor.archiveHint: Archived roles cannot be given to anyone new. People who hold it keep it until you change their roles.

grid.caption: Permissions by role
grid.stale: This role has changed. Reload and try again.

documents.upload: Upload documents and ask customers for papers
documents.manage: Replace, remove and manage all documents

settings.manage: Change company settings, catalog and rates

company.intro: These details appear on quotations, invoices, statutory reports and WhatsApp messages.
company.shortAddressHint: Used where space is tight, like report footers.
company.phonesHint: One per line. The first is shown on documents.
company.signatoryHint: Printed under the signature and stamp on quotations and reports.
company.signatoryMissing: The signatory's name is still blank, so documents will print without it.

starter.title: Starter values: review and replace
starter.rates: These rates were filled in so pricing works on day one. They are not OneOhm's rates. Check every figure and save to make this OneOhm's own rate card.
starter.products: {count, plural, one {# product is} other {# products are}} from the starter catalog, not OneOhm's real price list. Edit them with your real products and prices, or archive them.

products.intro: Every product a quotation can use. Each panel is tagged DCR or non-DCR, which decides subsidy eligibility.
products.emptyBody: Add the products OneOhm sells so quotations can use them.

dialog.name: Name
dialog.dcrHint: Only DCR panels qualify for PM Surya Ghar subsidy.
dialog.technologyHint: For example Mono PERC bifacial or TOPCon.
dialog.datasheetLater: Save the product first, then add its datasheet.

discoms.title: DISCOMs
discoms.intro: Each DISCOM has its own task set and report formats. Expected days drive the waiting alerts on projects.

subsidy.title: Subsidy rules
subsidy.intro: PM Surya Ghar central financial assistance as the price engine applies it. A change is a new version from a start date; versions already in force stay as history, and accepted quotations keep the subsidy they were accepted with.
subsidy.earlier: {count, plural, one {# earlier version} other {# earlier versions}}

form.intro: The price engine uses the newest version that has started. Until this one starts you can still change or withdraw it.
form.validFromHint: Today or later. Earlier dates are history.
form.slabsHint: Each slab pays its amount for every kW inside it. Leave the last slab's end empty for no upper limit.
form.noSlabs: No slabs: customers in this category get no subsidy.
form.perHouseholdHint: Eligible capacity is at most this for each home in the society.

withdrawDialog.title: Withdraw this version?
withdrawDialog.body: The {category} rule starting {date} has not come into force, so no quotation has used it. The rule in force now stays.

impact.title: Open quotations to review
impact.asOf: Under the rules in force on {date}
impact.summary: {checked, plural, =0 {There are no draft or sent quotations to check.} one {Checked # draft or sent quotation:} other {Checked # draft or sent quotations:}} {changed, plural, =0 {none would change.} one {# would change.} other {# would change.}}
impact.note: Each one is priced afresh and compared with the subsidy it saved. Nothing is changed here: revise a quotation to update it. Accepted quotations always keep their subsidy.
impact.noneBody: Every draft and sent quotation keeps the same expected subsidy under these rules.

workforce.title: Workforce rules
workforce.intro: How leave, attendance and check-in location work. These rules guide requests and check-ins; people still decide every approval.

leaveKinds.title: Kinds of leave
leaveKinds.description: What people can ask for, and how many days of each a year.
leaveKinds.perYear: {count, plural, one {# day a year} other {# days a year}}
leaveKinds.removeHint: Requests already made keep their kind. Changes apply when you save.

dialog.description: Kept with your other changes until you save the page.
dialog.label: Name
dialog.labelError: Give it a name of at least 2 letters.
dialog.keyHint: Lowercase letters and underscores, stored on every request.
dialog.keyFixed: Fixed once requests can use it.
dialog.keyError: Use 2 to 30 lowercase letters or underscores.
dialog.keyTaken: Another kind already uses this short name.
dialog.daysHint: Whole days a person can take in a calendar year.

workingDay.title: Working week
workingDay.description: The days people work, and when the working day starts and ends.
workingDay.offDays: Weekly off: {days}. Leave on these days is not counted.
workingDay.graceHint: Check-ins later than the start plus these minutes are marked late.

location.title: Location at check-in
location.description: Whether check-in and check-out note where the phone is, to compare with your authorised places.
location.captureOn: Used only for people who have agreed to share it.
location.privacyConsent: Each person agrees in the app before anything is shared, and can stop sharing at any time.
location.privacyMoments: The location is read only at the moment of a day or site check-in or check-out and when a site photo is taken, in working hours, never in between.
location.privacyRetention: Coordinates are deleted after {days} days; the times stay.
location.autoCheckIn: Check in automatically at the first site check-in
location.autoCheckInOn: The day’s first site or service check-in also starts the working day, for people who mark attendance.
location.autoCheckInOff: People check in for the day themselves.

byRole.title: By role
byRole.description: Switch location on or off for whole roles. A person’s own setting in Team wins; a role switched off wins over one switched on.
byRole.label: Location for {role}

places.title: Authorised places
places.description: Offices and yards check-ins are measured against. Changes here save straight away.
places.emptyBody: Add the office so check-ins can say whether people were there.
places.activeHint: Only places that are switched on are used for check-ins.

dialog.description: Check-ins within the radius count as inside.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.coordinatesHint: In Google Maps, right-click the spot and click the numbers to copy them.
dialog.activeHint: Switch off to stop using it without losing it.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Skills people hold and task templates can ask for, such as a wiring licence or working at height.
skills.summary: {people, plural, =0 {Nobody has it yet} one {# person} other {# people}}{about, select, other { · {about}}}
skills.hint: Tick skills on each person in Team. Switching a skill off keeps it on people but stops new use.

dialog.description: The name shows on people and task templates.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.aboutHint: For example: holds a valid wireman licence for AC work.

workload.title: Workload
workload.description: How many open tasks one person should carry. Team shows a warning when someone is at or over it.
workload.limitHint: 0 means no limit. People can have their own limit in Team.

taskTemplates.title: Task templates
taskTemplates.intro: Every new project gets these tasks, in this order, when its conditions match. Changes apply to projects created from now on; tasks already on projects stay as they are.
taskTemplates.when: Day {offset} · {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

sheet.title: Task name
sheet.descriptionHint: One or two plain lines on what to get done. Shown on the task in the app and on the web.
sheet.keyHint: Lowercase words joined by underscores. It cannot change later.
sheet.dependsOnHint: This task opens when these are done.
sheet.conditionsHint: Leave everything open to add the task to every project.
sheet.discomsHint: No DISCOM picked means every DISCOM.
sheet.discomsNone: No DISCOMs yet. Add them under DISCOMs & subsidy.
sheet.discomUnlisted: No longer in your DISCOM list
sheet.capturesHint: What the person fills in when they finish. These feed the reports.
sheet.reportsHint: Saved to the project documents once this task is done and the report's details are complete.
sheet.approval: Needs approval before it counts as done
sheet.reviewerHint: Nobody approves their own work while someone else can.
sheet.customerVisible: Customers see this step in their app
sheet.notifyCustomer: Send the customer a WhatsApp message
sheet.customerTitleHint: Required when the customer is told. For example “Net meter fitted”.
sheet.notifyManager: Tell the project manager when it is done
sheet.skillHint: People in the role with this skill get the task first; if none is free, anyone in the role.
sheet.checklistHint: One line per check. The person ticks each before finishing. New projects get this list; tasks already made keep theirs.

recipientOptions.customer_and_family: The customer and family members with app access

sheet.attachmentHint: A report, or the newest paper in a folder. Pick “Update with a link” as the message.

messageTemplates.title: WhatsApp messages
messageTemplates.intro: Messages OneOhm starts must use templates approved in Meta's WhatsApp Manager. Match each one here: the template name, its language, and which detail fills '{{'1'}}', '{{'2'}}' and so on.

names.stage_rating_request: Ask the customer to rate a stage

dialog.title: Edit {name}
dialog.languageHint: For example en, hi or mr.
dialog.previewHint: Copy it from WhatsApp Manager, with '{{'1'}}', '{{'2'}}' where details go.
dialog.localHint: Approved in WhatsApp Manager in Marathi (mr) or Hindi (hi), with the same details in the same order. Customers who chose that language get it; everyone else gets the English one.
dialog.extrasApproved: Meta approved the version with file and buttons
dialog.extrasApprovedHint: Turn on only after Meta approves it. If messages fail, turn it off.

activity.title: Activity log
activity.intro: Important actions, document changes and money events, with who did them and when. Sign-ins show every try, so you can spot someone guessing passwords.

paymentPlans.title: Payment terms
paymentPlans.intro: How customers pay across a project: each payment is a share of the price and falls due at an event. New projects use the default unless someone picks another plan. Projects already created keep their amounts.
paymentPlans.dialogHint: The shares must make 100%. A bank loan's share is always added as its own payment.
paymentPlans.name: Name
paymentPlans.active: Offer these terms on new projects

rewards.intro: Everything OneOhm gives for good work, in one place. Points are a thank-you to staff; referral rewards, reseller commission and project bonuses are money, and each is approved before anyone is paid.

points.title: What earns points
points.description: Points go to staff only; partner crews and resellers are paid, not scored. Set 0 to stop giving that kind of points.
points.caption: What earns points, how many, and who approves them

events.onTimeTaskDetail: For whoever hands the task in by its due date. Days waiting on the customer, bank or DISCOM, and approved leave, are added first. Late work earns nothing and loses nothing.
events.firstTimeRightDetail: For tasks with an approval step, approved without being sent back.
events.stageRating: Named on a 4 or 5 star stage rating
events.stageRatingDetail: Suggested for each staff member the customer names on a survey, installation or switch-on rating.
events.recognitionMaxDetail: Given with a reason, never for the manager's own work. This is the most one recognition can give.

meaning.title: What points mean
meaning.description: A simple, fair record of dependable work.
meaning.where: Team → Points lists everyone's points this month and in all, the suggestions waiting for a manager, and recent points.
meaning.app: In the OneOhm app, each person sees their own points, history and achievements, such as five tasks on time in a row or the 500 club.
meaning.noCash: Points have no cash value and are not part of pay. Money for good work is a project bonus, below.
meaning.fair: Only verified work counts: nobody gives points to themselves, and delays caused by customers, banks or the DISCOM never count against anyone.

other.title: Other rewards
other.description: These pay money. Each has its own settings; this is how they stand today.
other.unavailable: Could not load this just now.
other.referralPerReferral: Customers earn {amount} for each friend who goes solar, {event}.
other.referralPerKw: Customers earn {amount} per kW a friend installs, {event}.
other.referralOffDetail: Switched off. Codes still work and referrals are recorded, but nothing is earned.
other.commissionDetail: The usual rule: {rule}. A reseller can have their own rule.
other.bonusesDetail: Proposed for good work on a project under Team → Bonuses. Someone who approves payments decides each one, within their limit in Approvals; finance then pays it.

referrals.title: Refer and earn
referrals.intro: Customers share their own code on WhatsApp. When a referred friend's project reaches the event you choose, the reward is earned and waits for finance to approve and pay it. Changes apply to rewards earned from now on.

reward.title: Reward
reward.description: What a customer earns for each friend who goes solar.
reward.activeHint: When off, codes still work and referrals are recorded, but nothing is earned.
reward.amountHint: Paid once for each referred project.
reward.amountPerKwHint: A 3.27 kW system at ₹500 per kW earns ₹1,635.
reward.eventHint: The referred friend's project must reach this step.

campaign.title: Campaign and limits
campaign.description: Referrals registered from the start day count. Rewards never go over the budget or a customer's limit.
campaign.usageNoBudget: {committed} committed so far, {paid} paid. No budget set.

eligibility.title: Who qualifies
eligibility.description: The kinds of project that earn a reward, and where friends send the code.
eligibility.allTypes: None ticked: every project type qualifies.
eligibility.someTypes: Only the ticked project types earn a reward.
eligibility.shareNumberHint: Leave empty to use the company number, {number}.
eligibility.shareNumberNone: Leave empty to use the company's first phone number.

leadSteps.intro: Name the steps a lead goes through, in your own words. Each step sits inside one of four fixed stages that OneOhm uses for automation: sending a quotation moves a lead to Quoted, and an accepted quotation wins it.

about.new: Just captured, not yet spoken to.
about.contacted: Spoken to; working out the need and the site.
about.survey_scheduled: A site survey is booked or done.
about.quoted: A quotation went out. Sending one moves leads here.

leadSteps.leads: {count, plural, =0 {No open leads} one {# open lead} other {# open leads}}

dialog.name: Step name
dialog.nameHint: For example: Negotiation, Loan check, Site visit done.

requirements.intro: The papers every project checklist asks for, and which projects need each one. Switching a paper off takes it off every checklist; files already uploaded stay.

dialog.description: Any file in the chosen folder counts as this paper.
dialog.label: Paper
dialog.folderHint: Files in this folder count as this paper.
dialog.fromCustomerHint: The team can ask the customer for it from the checklist.
dialog.discomsHint: Comma separated, for example MSEDCL. Empty means every DISCOM.

rules.unsaved: You have changes that are not saved.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.intro: When customers are reminded to pay, when the team gets its morning list, and how early lead follow-ups are flagged. Changes apply from the next run.

payments.title: Payment reminders
payments.description: Sent to the customer on WhatsApp while a payment stays unpaid.
payments.graceHint: Days after the payment falls due. 0 sends it on the due day.
payments.repeatHint: Until it is paid. Each reminder goes once.
payments.preview: For a payment due on {due}: reminders on {first}, {second}, {third} and so on until it is paid.

daily.title: Daily messages
daily.description: Sent once a day at these times, India time.
daily.staffHint: Each person's overdue work, today's work and follow-ups.
daily.ownerHint: Yesterday's work and money, and on Mondays the week.

followUps.title: Lead follow-ups
followUps.description: The lead owner gets an alert ahead of each follow-up date.
followUps.preview: {days, plural, =0 {A follow-up planned for {date} is reminded that morning at {time}.} one {A follow-up planned for {date} is reminded on {remind} at {time}, a day before.} other {A follow-up planned for {date} is reminded on {remind} at {time}, # days before.}}

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp at night
whatsapp.description: When a customer writes outside 9:30 am to 6:30 pm and a person has their chat.
whatsapp.nightReply: Send one calm reply at night
whatsapp.nightReplyPreview: The customer gets once a night, in their language: “Thank you. We reply from 9:30 am to 6:30 pm. Your message is with Asha.”

assignment.title: Assignment rules
assignment.intro: How a new project's tasks find a person. Crew work always goes to the project's contractor, and tasks marked critical still wait for a manager to confirm the person.

who.title: Who gets the next task
who.description: Among the people in the task's role.

explain.least_busy: The person with the fewest open tasks gets it, so work spreads to whoever has room.
explain.round_robin: The person who was given work longest ago gets it, so everyone in the role takes turns.

checks.title: Who is skipped or preferred
checks.description: People marked unavailable in Team are always skipped.
checks.skipLeaveHint: Someone with approved leave on the task's days is passed over.
checks.preferSkillHint: When a task template names a skill, someone who has it comes first.
checks.teamFirstHint: When a project has a named team, its tasks go to them before anyone else.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.intro: Who must say yes before money moves or a price changes, and when a waiting approval goes up to the owner. Everything waiting for someone shows in their Today → Waiting for my approval.
approvals.limitHint: ₹0 means each one needs someone who approves payments.

discount.title: Discounts
discount.description: Set with the rate card, shown here so every approval rule is in one place.
discount.rule: A salesperson may give up to {percent}% off without approval. A bigger discount waits for someone who approves discounts before the quotation is sent.

bill.title: Bills to pay
bill.description: Vendor, contractor and staff bills before they are paid.
bill.limit: Accounts may approve bills up to
bill.within: Bills up to {amount} can be approved by people who record payments. Bigger bills need someone who approves payments.
bill.always: Every bill needs someone who approves payments.

bonus.title: Project bonuses
bonus.description: Bonuses proposed for a project team.
bonus.limit: Managers may approve bonuses up to
bonus.within: Bonuses up to {amount} in total can be approved by managers who manage people. Bigger ones need someone who approves payments.
bonus.always: Every bonus needs someone who approves payments.

refunds.title: Refunds and cancellations
refunds.description: Money back to a customer, a reversed payment or a cancelled tax invoice.
refunds.rule: Only someone who approves payments can do these, whatever the amount.

waiting.title: Waiting too long
waiting.description: Approvals that wait are raised to the owner once.
waiting.daysHint: Counted from the day it was asked for.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.intro: What the command centre counts as late or coming up, and how many items its lists show.

late.title: When something is late
late.description: Before this, it does not show as a problem.

ahead.title: How far ahead to look
ahead.description: Deadlines, installs, bills due and material checks.

lists.title: List sizes
lists.description: The most items each list shows; counts always include everything.

fields.riskLateDays: Task counts as at risk after (days late)
fields.riskLateDaysHint: {count, plural, one {Shown in What could slip from 1 day late.} other {Shown in What could slip from # days late.}}
fields.paymentLateDays: Payment needs a reminder call after (days)
fields.discomWaitDaysHint: A task waiting on the DISCOM this long becomes an action.
fields.dueSoonDaysHint: Deadlines, installs and bills due in this window.
fields.materialLookAheadDaysHint: Projects short of material for work due in this window.
fields.risksShownHint: Late work first, then waiting, then unowned.

projectTypes.title: Project types
projectTypes.intro: The kinds of project OneOhm builds. Rename them, describe them for the team, or switch one off so no new project of that kind can start. Projects already running carry on.
projectTypes.newKind: A brand-new kind of project needs its own task list and rules, so ask for it to be added; task templates already know every kind listed here.

dialog.title: Edit {name}
dialog.description: The name and note show to the team when they create projects.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.offeredHint: {count, plural, =0 {No projects of this kind yet.} one {1 project of this kind keeps running either way.} other {# projects of this kind keep running either way.}}

automation.title: Automation runs
automation.intro: Every automatic job OneOhm runs: reminders, escalations, summaries, messages and payment checks. Failures come first; the ones that are safe to run again have a retry.
automation.allWell: Everything ran as planned in the last 7 days.
automation.failedWeek: {count, plural, one {1 run failed in the last 7 days.} other {# runs failed in the last 7 days.}}
automation.empty: No runs yet. Jobs record here from their next run.
automation.kept: Runs are kept for 30 days. Payment and payout checks that run every few minutes are listed only when they did something or failed.
automation.retryQueued: Queued to run again within a minute
